item.title: France's Socialists in turmoil over alliances with LFI as presidential race looms
item.description: Socialist leader Olivier Faure has faced criticism from internal rivals, including former president François Hollande, over the party's 'zigzagging' on alliances with the radical-left La France Insoumise.

item.title: Trump steps back from his own Iran ultimatum
item.description: The US president postponed his deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, claiming talks are underway with the regime, which Iranian officials deny.

item.title: French judge probes former EU border chief for complicity in crimes against humanity
item.description: Fabrice Leggeri, now a far-right member of the European Parliament, was accused of tolerating pushbacks of asylum seekers during a seven-year spell as Frontex chief that began in 2015.

item.title: In southern Lebanon, civilians are trapped after Israel destroys bridges
item.description: The Israeli military is seeking to isolate southern Lebanon, a Hezbollah stronghold, from the rest of the country. Now, only one access route connects Tyre's remaining 20,000 residents and displaced people to the capital.

item.title: Iran names ex-IRGC commander to succeed Larijani as security chief
item.description: After Supreme National Security Council head Ali Larijani was killed in an Israeli strike, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, a long-serving former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander, has been appointed to succeed him.

item.title: From afar, American students in France feel the shockwaves of Trump
item.description: As academic freedom declines in the US, some young people are choosing France to pursue master's and doctoral degrees. Yet, between delayed scholarships, intrusive questions and stereotypes, their experience remains shaken by the latest developments in their country.

item.title: Danish PM Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats lead election but fall short of majority
item.description: With all votes counted, the left-wing bloc was credited with 84 seats in the 179-seat parliament and the right with 77. Frederikson, a favorite going into elections, has been praised for her leadership after fending off US President Trump's repeated demands to annex Greenland, a Danish autonomous territory.

item.title: The serial-poisoning mother and daughter inspired by 'Breaking Bad'
item.description: Castor beans, wolfsbane, antifreeze, rat poison: Carole D. and Amélie D. considered every possible method to poison the former's partner, Enrique B. The two women are set to stand trial before a criminal court in western France starting March 25.

item.title: Meta found liable for endangering children in New Mexico in 'historic' verdict
item.description: The tech giant was ordered to pay $375 million in damages by a Santa Fe jury, which found the company prioritized profits over safety and concealed what it knew about the harmful effects of its apps.

item.title: French conservatives to vote on whether to hold a presidential primary
item.description: Les Républicains will put three options for selecting their presidential election candidate to a vote of party members.

item.title: Population's cadmium overexposure requires urgent action, French food agency tells government
item.description: In a report published on Wednesday, France's National Agency for Food Safety recommends drastically reducing levels of this carcinogenic metal in phosphate fertilizers and limiting the consumption of cereals, bread and pasta.

item.title: French left's presidential primary threatened by Socialists' infighting
item.description: Socialist leader Olivier Faure has faced internal backlash over local election alliances with the radical La France Insoumise party. The idea of a broader left-wing primary is meeting growing opposition within his party.

item.title: 'Trump would benefit from rereading Obama's 2015 speech on Iran'
item.description: The US president belatedly realized that the military option carried significant risks. He did not rely on his administration's recognized experts on Iran, notes Le Monde columnist Gilles Paris.

item.title: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune strengthens his grip on power
item.description: On Wednesday, the Algerian Parliament is set to adopt a constitutional revision that increases the president's powers, particularly over judicial appointments and elections.

item.title: 'In Paris, the ideal of urban transformation clearly resonated with voters'
item.description: Emmanuel Grégoire, the Socialist mayor-elect at the head of a left-wing and environmentalist coalition, now faces two main challenges: responding to the anxiety of Parisians who fear being driven out of their city by the high cost of living and pursuing a policy of solidarity with Greater Paris, writes economist Frédéric Gilli.
